payload.props_realized:
The frame records TWO value props with a need register N1-N12. Every one now has at least one story.

PROP 1 — THE AGENT WALKING THE LOOP. Realized by S2, S3, S4, S8.
  N1 read any source the process mandates — S2 slides 1-3, UC-B ext 2b.
  N2 find things without four attempts, WITH CONTEXT — S2 slide 4, UC-B step 3.
  N3 know the rules that bind this step — S8 (the law minted this afternoon), UC-H. NEW: this was the gap that reopened the milestone.
  N4 edit many sites at once — S2 slide 5, UC-C.
  N5 search what shipped — S2 slide 3, UC-B ext 2a.

PROP 2 — THE OWNER WHO OWNS AN ITERATION THEY DID NOT WATCH. Realized by S1, S5, S6, S7, S9, S10.
  N6 mechanical checks are mechanical — S5 slide 5, UC-F step 2.
  N7 a lint never parks an unattended run — S5 slide 3, UC-F ext 2a.
  N8 the record survives carelessness — S9 (the tag that was deleted), UC-I. NEW.
  N9 the audit distinguishes computed from asserted — S10 (who actually checked this), UC-J. NEW.
  N10 a gate is reviewed, not just filled — S1, UC-A.
  N11 a reopen verdict does something — S1 slide 5, S6, UC-A ext 6a.
  N12 the red-team round is adversarial — S1 slide 4, UC-A step 5.

Twelve needs, twelve covered. Three stories (S3 engine promotion, S4 refusals, S7 expanding identifiers) realize a prop but no numbered need, because the register predates the owner rulings that produced them; each carries a REGISTER NOTE saying so, and M3 sources those requirements to the story and the ruling rather than inventing a need to hang them on.
payload.stories_generalized:
Ten stories, ten use cases, every story inside one:
  S1 → UC-A (close a gate under review) · S2 → UC-B + UC-C · S3 → UC-D · S4 → UC-E · S5 → UC-F · S6 → UC-A ext 6a · S7 → UC-G · S8 → UC-H · S9 → UC-I · S10 → UC-J.
No use case without a story behind it. Every extension hangs off a numbered step. No UI mechanics: re-read the ten scenarios looking for tool names and found none — the steps say 'the machine refuses', never a clause code or a tool name.
One addition the re-fill made that the first pass lacked: UC-A gained ext 6b (a live offer for a gate whose verdict is reopen must be DISMISSED, not left standing), which came directly from doing it — the previous fill of this gate produced an offer that had to be withdrawn by hand.
payload.roles_covered:
All six roles from map_stakeholders appear as actor or stakeholder:
  THE OWNER — UC-G primary stakeholder, UC-J PRIMARY ACTOR (new: the owner was a stakeholder everywhere and the actor nowhere, which is a strange shape for a system whose whole purpose is their trust), UC-A stakeholder, UC-H stakeholder.
  THE WALKING AGENT — primary actor in UC-B, UC-C, UC-D, UC-E, UC-G, UC-H.
  THE PARALLEL AGENT — UC-D's named stakeholder and the reason for its refusals.
  THE REVIEWING AGENT — primary actor in UC-A.
  THE FUTURE READER — UC-I PRIMARY ACTOR (new), UC-A stakeholder.
  THE ENGINE AS SHARED JUDGE — UC-D exists to protect it.
Six tensions named with reasoning at map_stakeholders, none left as 'none found': T1 walking vs reviewing agent · T2 walking vs parallel agent · T3 owner vs agent over precision · T4 engine-as-judge vs its builder · T5 future reader vs walking agent over rewrites · T6 owner vs engine over dependencies.
payload.excluded_stated:
Yes, at draw_context, binding and system-level, each with its reason: no authoring of method CONTENT; no board, browser or phone work; no turning items into ledger nodes; no general-purpose agent shell; no retiring the predecessor system; no second mechanism for one job EXCEPT where the jobs are genuinely two; and no answering a tooling gap by keeping the human in the loop.
Re-checked against the three NEW use cases, since new work is where an excluded list earns its keep:
  UC-H (rules arrive in the packet) — DELIVERS existing rules; it does not author or amend any. Inside the boundary.
  UC-I (recover a careless record) — uses version-control history, which is a named neighbour, not new machinery. Inside.
  UC-J (audit computed vs asserted) — lands on the excluded 'no items as nodes' line and STAYS on the right side of it: it distinguishes a computed check from an asserted one, which needs no item to be a node. The part that WOULD need it (computing the model-adherence check itself) stays deferred, per UC-F ext 2a.
payload.examples_formulated:
The formulated examples are the numbered scenario steps and extensions across the ten use cases, plus the slides they generalize — the examples' birth per meth-examples-checkable, roles now and nodes later.
Those that must become checkable at validation, named so none is quietly dropped:
  UC-A step 2 / ext 2a — every gate form carries the four rounds as REQUIRED and a blank round is refused. Mechanically checkable across every gate in the machine.
  UC-A ext 6a — a reopen re-activates the cone, supersedes rather than deletes, AND leaves the downstream gate reachable. That last clause is new, and it is there because the first live reopen deadlocked the machine on exactly this.
  UC-A ext 6b — a reopen verdict leaves no live offer standing.
  UC-B step 3 — a match carries context in the SAME call.
  UC-C ext 2a — one bad edit in a batch writes nothing.
  UC-D ext 4b / 4c — a red suite promotes nothing and NAMES the failures; a suite that runs nothing counts as red.
  UC-E ext 2a — absent and explicitly-empty are different.
  UC-F ext 2a — an uncomputable check defers with its reason and never passes.
  UC-H ext 2a — a rule that declares no state it applies to is REPORTABLE as unattached.
  UC-I ext 2a — evidence is reachable by hash with the tag and branch gone.
  UC-J step 2 / ext 3a — origin is distinguishable without reading prose, and a computed label with no fact behind it is not credited.
Evidence sides stay empty until validation.
payload.verify_round:
BUILT IT RIGHT. The two re-walked states opened and read; the two untouched ones re-checked for consistency with the new material rather than assumed.

1. write_stories (second fill) — read. Claim: ten slideshows, each realizing a NAMED prop, killers marked. Verified: two props stated with their full need registers at the top; every story header names its prop and its needs; four killers marked (S1, S2, S3, S8) with a why-killer line each. The three previously-unstoried needs each have a story: N3→S8, N8→S9, N9→S10. The first fill's defect — eight invented 'props' — is gone, and the three register-orphan stories now carry an explicit REGISTER NOTE instead of being silently unmapped. HOLDS.

2. generalize_use_cases (second fill) — read. Claim: every story covered, extensions numbered off steps, no UI mechanics. Verified story by story. Checked the three new use cases hardest, since they are the ones with no prior review: UC-H has five steps and three extensions, all hanging off numbered steps; UC-I has three steps and four extensions, including the silent-failure case (ext 2c) which is the whole risk of that need; UC-J has five steps and three extensions, and its ext 2a ties back to UC-F ext 2a so the deferral story and the audit story cannot drift apart. HOLDS.

3. draw_context — NOT reopened, re-read anyway, because the new use cases could have crossed its boundary without anyone noticing. Checked each of the seven excluded items against UC-H, UC-I and UC-J. All three are inside; the finding is recorded in excluded_stated. HOLDS.

4. map_stakeholders — NOT reopened, re-read. The new use cases changed the role picture in a way worth stating: the owner and the future reader were stakeholders everywhere and primary actors nowhere until UC-J and UC-I. The roles were right; their standing improved. HOLDS.

5. THE M1 FRAME — frame_delta-2 re-read for the corrected N2 pass line, and frame_delta-1 (SUPERSEDED) re-read for the full N1-N9 register that this whole review is measured against. Superseded evidence used as a working source for the second time in one gate.

6. THE MACHINE ITSELF — verified beyond the evidence, because this gate's own reopen exposed a defect. The reopen deadlocked the walk: gate_inputs is a three-way join and the fuel from its two untouched arms had been consumed at the first activation, so the gate became unreachable — silently, with no error and no legal move. Fixed, covered by four tests with red observed, promoted to trunk (b91bc8e, 220 passed / 0 failed in trunk), and the live instance repaired by re-arming exactly the two edges the fixed code would have re-armed. Logged as note-a2d5f31c0a3c. I record it HERE rather than only in the retro because this gate's verdict depends on a reopen having actually worked, and until an hour ago it did not.

A BLESS IS NOT PROOF: the earlier fills of draw_context and map_stakeholders were treated as claims to re-read, not as settled facts, even though they were never reopened.
payload.validate_round:
BUILT THE RIGHT THING — against the frame, the vision and the need register.

WHAT IS MISSING: nothing in the register. All twelve needs have a story and a use case; the three that drove the reopen (N3, N8, N9) are closed by S8/UC-H, S9/UC-I, S10/UC-J. I checked each against its PASS LINE rather than its title, because a story can nod at a need's subject and still miss what it asks:
  N3's pass line is that a packet at a state to which a law applies CARRIES it, resolved, without the agent searching. UC-H step 3 says exactly resolved-not-pointer, and ext 2a covers the law that declares no state.
  N8's pass line is that after deleting every tag locally, a closed iteration's evidence is still reachable from trunk by hash. UC-I ext 2a is that sentence as a scenario.
  N9's pass line is that a computed check is distinguishable from an asserted one WITHOUT reading the prose. UC-J step 2 says without the prose being read; ext 3a closes the loophole where an origin label carries no fact.

WHAT IS WRONG: nothing outstanding. The first pass's two defects — invented props, unstoried needs — are both corrected, and the correction is visible in the record rather than smoothed over.

WHAT IS OUT OF SCOPE: nothing. The three new use cases were checked against the binding excluded list, item by item; UC-J was the one that could have crossed it and does not.

ASKS NO CHECK COVERED — the drift indicator. Still three (engine promotion, refusals, expanding identifiers), all from owner rulings issued after the frame was written, all now carrying an explicit register note. This is a stale REGISTER, not drifting work: the rulings are the authority and the register simply has not caught up. Handled by sourcing at M3. I considered adding N13-N15 to the frame and rejected it — amending M1 to make M2 tidier would re-walk the whole milestone for a bookkeeping gain.

AGAINST THE GOAL SYSTEM. G5 (a review happens because something asks for it) is doing visible work: this milestone has now produced three findings that came from being ASKED rather than from diligence — the invented props, the three unstoried needs, and the reopen deadlock, the last of which was only discovered because the verdict of the first review was carried out. G1 (the lane wins on merit) took a real hit: the reopen cost a full re-walk of two states plus an engine fix. That is the friction G5's conflict with G1 predicted, and the ruling stands — scale to size, but say so rather than skipping.
payload.redteam_round:
THE OPPOSING CASE, argued before endorsing.

CASE AGAINST PASSING — steelmanned, in increasing strictness.

FIRST, THE WEAK FORM: the three new stories were written by the same author who missed them, minutes after being told they were missing. They may be thin — written to satisfy a checklist rather than to describe anything real. REBUTTED, with a test rather than an assurance: each of the three was checked against its need's PASS LINE, not its title, and the pass lines are specific enough to fail a thin story (a deleted tag, a resolved rule rather than a pointer, a distinction visible without reading prose). A story that merely name-dropped the need would not survive that check. UC-I ext 2c in particular — the silent-failure case — is not the kind of detail a box-ticking story invents.

SECOND, STRICTER: the gate is now passing on its SECOND attempt, and a second attempt has a known failure mode — the reviewer has already spent its scepticism and wants to move on. The first review reopened; a second reopen would look like thrashing, and that pressure is real and unmeasured. REBUTTED ONLY PARTLY, and I will not overclaim: the guard I actually have is that the same pass-line check that produced the first verdict was run again the same way, and this time every need clears it. But I cannot prove I was as sceptical the second time. What I can say is that this round found a NEW defect the first round did not — the reopen deadlock — which is weak evidence that scrutiny did not simply collapse.

THIRD, STRICTEST: the deepest objection is that this gate is reviewing a milestone whose purpose is to describe a system that includes THE REVIEW ITSELF. The review is judging its own specification, and a defect in the review's design would be invisible to exactly this instrument. This is not resolvable by trying harder. What can be done, and is: the specification is written so its claims are MECHANICALLY checkable later (UC-A step 2 is a machine-checkable property over every gate in the machine, not a promise about behaviour), so M8's validation can catch what M2's review structurally cannot. The honest statement is that this gate's verdict is worth less than the lint that will check it, and the specification is deliberately shaped to make that lint possible.

KILL-CRITERION for PASS: that a need's pass line is not actually reachable by its story's use case — i.e. the coverage is nominal. Looked for it by walking all twelve pass lines against the scenario steps, not the story titles. Not met.
SECOND KILL-CRITERION: that the reopen which produced this second pass did not actually work, making the whole re-walk theatre. This one nearly fired — the reopen DEADLOCKED. It is met-and-repaired rather than not-met, and the repair is verified by the machine standing at gate_inputs with the join satisfied, by four tests with red observed before green, and by a green suite in trunk. Had I not checked, this gate would have passed on a re-walk that the machine could not actually have completed.
THIRD, on the other side — what would make a REOPEN wrong now: that a remaining gap is cheaper to close at M3 than by another re-walk. The remaining gap is the stale register, and it is bookkeeping: the requirements it would produce are already sourced to stories and rulings. Reopening M1 to add three needs would re-walk all of M2 for tidiness. Not proportionate.

CITED RUBRIC, not vibes: meth-gate-review's own purpose for this gate — the user-level picture stops here for judgment because requirements written on unblessed stories propagate garbage. The test is therefore whether M3 can now write a requirement for every need and trace it to a scenario step. It can, for all twelve.

HONEST WEAKNESS: unchanged from the first review and worth repeating rather than dropping once it has been said — I am the author of what I am red-teaming. The round binds form, not sincerity. Its value this time was that the second kill-criterion sent me to check whether the reopen had actually worked, and it had not.
payload.verdict:
PASS.

All five acceptance items are met: twelve needs across two props each realized by at least one story; ten stories each inside a use case; six roles covered with six tensions named; a binding excluded list that the three new use cases were checked against item by item; and the formulated examples named, with the ones that must become mechanically checkable listed rather than left implicit.

NO OVERRIDES. Nothing is blessed past an unmet criterion.

RECORDED WITH THE PASS, because a clean verdict should not hide what it cost:
- This gate reopened once, on its own review. The reopen was correct and the re-walk closed all three gaps.
- Carrying out that reopen exposed a defect in the machine: reopen deadlocked the walk by stranding this gate's three-way join. Fixed, covered by four tests with red observed first, promoted to trunk (b91bc8e, 220 passed / 0 failed in trunk), live instance repaired, logged as note-a2d5f31c0a3c. The gate's verdict depends on a reopen having worked, so it belongs here and not only in the retro.
- The need register is stale by three items — engine promotion, refusals over confident wrong answers, and expanding identifiers for a reader who cannot see them. All three come from owner rulings issued after the frame was written. M3 sources their requirements to the stories and the rulings. The M1 frame is deliberately NOT reopened for bookkeeping.

M3 may now write requirements on this picture.
